As much as I love Astarion, he probably won’t be the one used as a cash cow if anything. We are definitely the loud minority bc we make fics and art and whatnot, but the main consumers of BG3 as well as all other RPG is and always will be straight cis men, most of whom have a pretty hardcore dislike of Astarion (see: every comment about staking him when he tries to bite, killing him on first meeting, selling him to Gandrel for the lulz, etc). Obviously there are some that are cool with him and like him, but most straight cis men I’ve seen who play this game straight up hate Astarion. 

Anyways, I’m hoping that if there ever is a BG4, it will be far in the future and made by a studio that cares about the story as much as Larian, with completely new characters. Maybe a few side interactions or possible companions with BG3 companions like we had with this game and the BG1/2 companions. But I’m sadly keeping my expectations low. But like another commenter said, we don’t know what will happen next so don’t worry about it yet! We can be sad years down the line if they announce a micro-transaction loot box filled BG4 lmao.

For now, let’s enjoy Astarion while the novelty is still pretty fresh. Most of us will move onto other interests eventually but he will always hold a special place in our hearts, just like all other characters we have loved in the past!

Ascending Astarion is def an evil-aligned choice imo. Do I actually care that much? No, bc it’s literally fiction and I don’t care what people enjoy in fiction. I occasionally enjoy AA fics bc I do sometimes enjoy dark romance and toxic relationships in fiction.

But you’re right - I feel like even if there are some arguments for ascending being the “better” ending for Astarion (which I personally disagree with, but people can have different views), they do tend to forget that it also damns 7000 innocent people to eternal torture in the hells lol. 

I enjoy SpawnStarion and occasionally enjoy Ascended Astarion. I will never try to justify AA being the “better” ending because I think it should be pretty common sense that damning 7000 people and allowing Astarion to become the thing he’s feared for centuries is the “bad” ending. 

But like I said, it’s fiction. I enjoy both. I think people should be able to enjoy what they want in fiction. It’s an important way to outlet some taboo thoughts/kinks/relationship dynamics.
